brief: Tonight is Legs A, and it is your sixth training day in a row — the longest streak in this log. Tomorrow is a rest day, so this is the last card before you get one. First, yesterday: you beat the deadlift card. It asked for 245 for six three times and you pulled 255 for six twice. That is the step earned, and next Pull A opens at 255. Tonight the biggest change is the leg press. It has four sets on the plan and you have only ever used the first one as a build-up — 160, 160, 180 against top sets of 220, 220 and 240 — so tonight it is three sets, 180, 220 and 240, eight reps each, at three minutes of rest. That is what you did on 2 August minus the last set, and on day six, one day after four deadlift sets, asking for more than you managed on day four is the wrong direction. The recovery trainer also wanted the Bulgarian split squats dropped tonight. I overruled that. They are 17.5 in each hand, the lightest thing on the card, and they are the only single-leg work on a day that has not run in seventeen days — the saving came out of the leg press instead, where a set is worth four times as much. Three sets, nine, nine and eight: the third set is the whole point, because you have logged only two both times this lift has ever run. Train the weaker leg first and match it, never beat it, with the stronger one. If the first set is genuinely unsteady rather than just hard, stop the lift there — that is the recovery trainer's call and it is already made. Leg curls step up to 127.5 then 142.5 twice: you carried 142.5 for four sets of twelve on the 16th, so anything lighter tonight would be work you have already done, and the hamstring rest comes from three sets instead of four. Leg extensions both move to 150. Hips go to 105 and stay at 135. Calves stay at 300 but the reps go to thirteen, thirteen and twelve — the card had been asking fifteen, which you have never done at that weight. Cable crunches 60 for thirteen, hanging leg raises for thirteen. Three Yes/No cards are waiting on your plan screen, and one of them changes an answer I gave you yesterday — read that one properly before you tap.

flags.note: Sixth training day in a row, the longest in your log. Tomorrow is a rest day — six sessions will have run since your last one.
First Legs A since 2 August — seventeen days. Every weight on tonight's card is built from that session or from Legs B on the 16th.

The recovery trainer vetoed the Bulgarian split squats tonight on fatigue grounds — balance work, six days deep, never yet run at three sets. I overruled it and took the saving off the leg press instead. If the first set is unsteady rather than just hard, stop the lift there.

One of tonight's cards asks to move a leg-curl set off Legs B and onto Legs A. Yesterday I told you four sets on Legs B is right, and no new Legs B session has been logged since — the evidence has not changed, only the question has. It is your call, and No is a real answer.
Your deadlift beat the card on 18 August: 255 for six, twice, against an ask of 245. Next Pull A opens at 255.
On 18 August the hammer curls went on dumbbells because the cables were taken, so 35 and 30 are dumbbell numbers and are not being read as cable loads.

Still open, and I still cannot put it on a card: your core work is all spinal flexion — cable crunches and hanging leg raises — and there is no anti-rotation movement anywhere in the app's exercise list, so a Pallof press cannot be prescribed until that list is changed. Say the word and it gets added.
Meso 1 closes on 23 August and Meso 2 opens on the 24th. There is no back-off week in between.

proposals.why: On all three Legs A nights your first leg-press set has been a build-up - 160, 160 and 180 against top sets of 220, 220 and 240 - so the four sets the plan asks for are really three of work plus a ramp, and at three minutes of rest each this is the most expensive slot on your longest session; tonight's card already runs three, and this makes it the standing shape.

Legs A gives the front of your leg nine sets - leg press, split squats and extensions - against three of leg curl and no hinge at all, and on 2 August all three of those curl sets finished at the top of the range at 135 for fifteen, so this makes it four; the card below takes that same set off Legs B, so your week's hamstring total does not move.

Read this one carefully: yesterday I answered your written question by telling you four sets on Legs B is right, and no Legs B session has been logged since, so nothing new has happened - this is the program trainer asking a different question, whether that fourth set is better spent on Legs A where you have nine quad sets and no hinge at all, rather than on the one day you already deadlift-pattern with RDLs. Accepting moves the set; declining keeps four on Legs B exactly as I told you yesterday, and No is a real answer.

overrides.reason: Three sets tonight, not four. On 2 August you did 180, 220, 240 and 240 for eight reps each - the card would reprint those four weights asking ten reps on all of them, which you have never done at 240. This is day six of a streak and one day after four deadlift sets, so asking for more than you managed on day four is the wrong direction. Same weights, same eight reps, one less set.

Both times this lift has run you logged only two sets and topped out at nine reps, so the card asking 17.5 for three sets of ten is a target you have never come close to. Weight holds; the reps are set so all three sets finish, because finishing the third set is the actual progress here. Weaker leg first, then match it.

You finished all three sets at the top of the range on 2 August at 120, 135 and 135 for fifteen, which pays for the 7.5-lb step, and you have already carried 142.5 for four sets of twelve on 16 August - so restarting at 135 would be redoing work you have done. Thirteen at 142.5 is the step; the hamstring rest comes from three sets tonight instead of four.

You finished 142.5 at the top of the range and got 150 for fourteen on 2 August, up from 150 for eleven two weeks earlier, so 142.5 has nothing left to give and both sets move to 150. Fifteen on both is what buys the next step to 157.5.

Both sets hit fifteen at 97.5 on 2 August, the top of the range, which earns the 7.5-lb step to 105. Twelve is the honest landing after a jump - last time you stepped up here you came back down to thirteen and twelve before climbing again.

You stepped up to 135 on 2 August and got twelve and twelve, the bottom of the range, so the weight holds and the reps move by one. The card would ask fifteen twice, a three-rep jump on both sets in one night.

You carried 300 for three sets of twelve on 16 August, so 300 is the right pin - but the card copies that night forward and asks fifteen on all three, three more per set than you have ever done at this weight. The next leg-press pin is 320 and it only opens once 300 goes for fifteen.

Three sets of fifteen at 55 on 2 August earned the 5-lb step, and you took 60 for three sets of twelve on 16 August - reprinting 60 for twelve is an exact copy of three days ago and asks for nothing new. One more rep per set is the smallest real step, and fifteens across the board buy 65.

This is bodyweight, so reps are the only thing that can move, and you have opened with twelve and twelve in every leg session since 18 July because the card reprints twelve every time. Thirteen is the step, and the range now runs to fifteen.

dissent.progression: Keep four sets and step the reps to 10/9/9/8 - the lift is stalled because the card reprints a rep target he has never hit.
dissent.recovery: Cut to three sets at 180/220/240 for eight - sixth straight day, a day after four deadlift sets topping 255 for six.
dissent.why: Progression is right that the stall is the prescription, but its fix asks for thirty-six reps on day six when he managed thirty-two on day four of a shorter streak. That is more work than he has ever done at these pins, on his most tired night. Recovery's version keeps the 240 top set - nothing is lost from the top end - and takes the saving out of the one slot that costs three minutes of rest per set. The program seat, which never saw either argument, independently found the same thing: his first leg-press set has been a build-up on all three Legs A nights, so the fourth set is a ramp priced as work. Two seats arriving at three sets from opposite directions decided this.

dissent.progression: Three sets at 17.5 with reps set so all three finish - he has logged only two sets both times it has run.
dissent.recovery: Skip it tonight - vetoed on fatigue grounds; balance work on a sixth straight day, debuted at a new set count.
dissent.why: I overruled a fatigue veto, which I am allowed to do and do not do lightly. Three things decided it. The load is 17.5 in each hand, the lightest thing on the card, so the systemic cost recovery is worried about is not actually here - and I paid that cost anyway by ruling recovery's way on the leg press, where one set is worth four times as much. This is the only single-leg work on a day that has not run in seventeen days, and skipping it would be the third consecutive time the third set never happens. And the app has no way to remove a lift for one night: upholding the veto would have left a card on his phone asking for 17.5 for ten, three times, directly contradicting a note telling him not to do it. Recovery raised no pain and no injury, so this was mine to call, and the off-ramp it asked for is on the card in words: if the first set is unsteady rather than hard, stop there.

dissent.progression: Step to 127.5/142.5/142.5 - he topped the range on 2 August and has already carried 142.5 for four sets of twelve.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 2 August exactly at 120/135/135 - RDLs on the 16th and deadlifts yesterday.
dissent.why: Recovery's own report says the hamstring-overload case is weaker than it looks: RDL plus four curl sets followed by three more four days later has run twice before with no decay. What is left of its argument is streak length, and 135 does not answer that - it asks for less than he did three days ago at 142.5, four times over, which is not rest, it is a step backwards printed as caution. The real rest is the set count: three tonight against four on the 16th. So the load takes the step it earned and the volume takes the cut.
